channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-13
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 132 news received.

item.title: Jensen Huang Leaves Nvidia After Alleged Espionage Scandal
item.description: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang reportedly resigned with immediate effect after revelations about an affair with someone suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence. Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, while Nvidia shares fell more than 13% at the open.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Email, Teams and Intune
item.description: A Microsoft 365 outage on November 12 disrupted access to email, some Teams features and administration tools such as Intune. Microsoft cited server health-check failures and an overloaded server process.

item.title: United Airlines Blocks Unauthorized Personal AI Agents
item.description: United is restricting unauthorized personal AI agents, citing unintended purchases, account information exposure and regulatory obligations. Analysts note that the lack of consistent standards and the difficulty of distinguishing bots from customers complicate transaction automation.

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla Could Announce Merger as Early as December
item.description: According to Bloomberg, Elon Musk’s two companies could officially announce their combination in December or early 2027. The deal would be the largest acquisition in history, but it has not yet been confirmed.

item.title: Silicon Valley Prepares for a Future Without Jensen Huang
item.description: At a major artificial intelligence conference in Silicon Valley, investors and executives are considering a future without Jensen Huang.

item.title: Companies Must Decide Which AI Agents to Allow as Customers or Intermediaries
item.description: AI agents are already buying on behalf of customers, and companies must decide which ones to let access their information, offers and services. OpenAI is opening an official path for businesses in ChatGPT, while United Airlines is restricting unauthorized third-party agents; agentic commerce is thus becoming a distribution strategy.

item.title: Google’s 10-Minute AI Training Plan for Marketers
item.description: Google is offering a 10-minute artificial intelligence training plan for marketing teams.

item.title: How Many Physical Keys Should You Get for a Tesla?
item.description: An owner asks how many physical keys are recommended for a Tesla. One response also mentions using an Apple Watch as a backup key.

item.title: Anthropic Turns Claude Into an Active Participant in Video Meetings
item.description: Claude Meetings lets users add the assistant to video calls to follow discussions, take notes and begin certain tasks before the meeting ends. The service is rolling out on Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plans, with other platforms expected to follow.

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a More Efficient Version of Carbon
item.description: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is presented as a more efficient alternative to Google’s most powerful model and is now available with all plans.

item.title: Wispr Flow Turns Voice Dictation Into Polished Text Across All Apps
item.description: Wispr Flow lets users dictate text in WhatsApp, Slack, Gmail, ChatGPT or a browser, then removes hesitations, corrects grammar and formats the result. The tool is available on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, with free unlimited access on Android at launch.

item.title: OpenAI’s Personal Assistant Gets Faster Responses and Advanced Settings
item.description: OpenAI’s personal assistant was upgraded this week with faster responses and more customizable instructions.

item.title: Chatbots Sometimes Recommend Fake E-Commerce Sites
item.description: A Podqi test of where to buy products from 151 brands found that ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity sometimes direct users to impersonation or risky websites. Users are advised to verify a brand’s official address before making a purchase.

item.title: OpenAI Explains Why Its Models Are Hiding More of Their Reasoning
item.description: OpenAI’s safety team attributes the growing opacity of its models’ chain of thought to four stages of training, including architecture and reinforcement learning. This opacity results from trade-offs intended to improve performance and reduce computation.

item.title: Generative AI Use Is Growing Among Video Game Developers
item.description: According to the annual GDC Festival of Gaming survey, 40% of developers use generative AI at work, up from 36% in 2025. The figure reaches 70% at mobile studios, while parts of the industry publicly oppose it.

item.title: Cerebras Stock Jumps After Deal With Microsoft
item.description: The AI chipmaker beat quarterly expectations and signed a deal with Microsoft, which joins Amazon and Oracle among its cloud customers. The announcement supports alternatives to Nvidia, despite the stock still being down nearly half since its IPO.

item.title: OpenAI Creates an Official Business Space in ChatGPT
item.description: Businesses can now claim their presence in ChatGPT, update their information and publish Business Agents that customers can interact with. ChatGPT is thus evolving from a descriptive tool into a distribution channel for businesses.

item.title: AI Assistants Are Becoming the Upstream Interface for Banking Services
item.description: According to McKinsey, 74% of consumers who use AI for banking tasks rely on general-purpose assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Customers can therefore make a decision before even entering a bank’s environment.

item.title: ChatGPT Becomes a New Gateway to Businesses
item.description: OpenAI has launched Businesses in ChatGPT, allowing companies to manage their presence, product information and customer interactions in ChatGPT. Customer acquisition is thus beginning to shift away from company-controlled channels.

item.title: Huang’s Departure Alarms Investors Across the AI Sector
item.description: The Nvidia leader’s resignation is weakening the company’s stock and raising fears of repercussions for companies across the artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: Huang’s Departure Could Change the Outlook for Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: Nvidia’s planned $10 billion investment could be reassessed, while future chip deals could slow. The departure could also strengthen Anthropic’s position in Washington and its chip-diversification strategy.

item.title: OpenAI Security Officials Tricked by Fake Russian Agents
item.description: Three senior OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes on a video call with Russian scammers posing as Ukraine’s intelligence chief. OpenAI has opened an investigation and taken steps to prevent a recurrence.

item.title: Groups Call for a Freeze on New AI Models
item.description: Four nonprofit organizations asked a San Francisco judge to halt new frontier models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI.

item.title: OpenAI Reportedly Supports Bills Restricting China’s Access to AI Chips
item.description: OpenAI reportedly told lawmakers it would support bipartisan bills restricting China’s access to artificial intelligence chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Reportedly Six Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO reportedly attracted about six times more demand than the number of shares offered. During its roadshow, the company also said Claude had been ported to AMD GPUs in three days, compared with several months previously.

item.title: SpaceX Announces $74 Billion in AI Computing Sites
item.description: SpaceX announced $74 billion in investments in AI-dedicated computing sites, including a $50 billion site in Arizona and a $24 billion gas-powered complex near Starbase.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Personal Agents Now Support Custom Instructions
item.description: ChatGPT’s personal agents can now follow custom instructions, such as writing only in lowercase or displaying a draft before sending an email.

item.title: Could the Touchscreen MacBook Pro Replace the M5 iPad Pro?
item.description: The touchscreen MacBook Pro supports macOS apps and offers substantial memory and storage, but it does not work with the Apple Pencil. It starts at $2,899, compared with $999 for the M5 iPad Pro.

item.title: Jensen Huang Reveals the Risk of Building a Company Around a Single Leader
item.description: The sudden departure of Nvidia’s former CEO highlights the risks of relying on a single leader. Nvidia’s flat structure helped it move quickly, but also left the company exposed.

item.title: Jensen Huang Is Targeted by the Technology He Helped Create
item.description: The article revisits criticism aimed at Jensen Huang and the technology he helped bring to prominence.

item.title: AI Is Upending the Economics of Customer Loyalty
item.description: AI allows agents to compare prices, terms and products every day, revealing that some loyalty was largely based on customer inertia. Companies must determine whether customers stay for trust, experience and genuine differentiation, or simply because switching providers is difficult.

item.title: Instagram Launches a Web Tool for Creating Story Effects With Prompts
item.description: Effect Builder lets US creators aged 18 and over generate AI effects for Stories without design or programming skills. Published effects are reviewed and display their creator’s Instagram account.

item.title: Anthropic Introduces Fable 5.2, Faster and Less Expensive to Run
item.description: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 is up to 30% faster than version 5.1. Its standard price is 8 dollars per million input tokens and 40 dollars per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode.

item.title: Adobe and Disney Partner to Create Custom AI Models
item.description: Disney will use Adobe Firefly Foundry to create models trained on its own characters, environments and visual styles. Walt Disney Imagineering is already using them to develop theme parks, including turning sketches into rendered 2D concepts.

item.title: Meta Launches Muse Ember, Its Smallest AI Model
item.description: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest model, priced at 0.10 dollar per million input tokens. It is designed for high-volume agent tasks such as tool calls and long-document analysis.

item.title: Google Publishes a Guide to Get More From Gemini 4 Carbon
item.description: Google has published a guide for developers featuring five practical tips for getting better results from Gemini 4 Carbon on difficult problems.

item.title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok Bot 1.0 for Teams on Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description: SpaceXAI has launched Grok Bot 1.0, a teammate that works in Slack or Microsoft Teams. It can take on tasks without prompting and share memory across an organization.

item.title: Lessons From Large Companies on Moving Beyond the AI Pilot Era
item.description: The era of AI pilots is over. Executives from JPMorgan Chase, Gap, Estée Lauder and other companies share practical lessons for evolving workflows and demonstrating marketing ROI.

item.title: Why 82% of Executives Fail to See Marketing’s Value
item.description: A study examines why 82% of executives overlook the value of marketing.

item.title: AI Reduces Friction While Human Expertise Dispels Doubts
item.description: Andy Kurtzig, Pearl’s founder and CEO, explains how AI reduces friction and how human expertise helps resolve uncertainty.

item.title: Which Mobile Charger Should You Use at 110 V and 240 V for a Tesla?
item.description: A new Tesla owner is looking for the best portable charger that works at 110 V and 240 V, particularly for semi-remote areas far from Superchargers.

item.title: A Free Way to Listen to Radio and Music in a Tesla
item.description: The discussion concerns a solution for listening to radio and music for free in a Tesla.

item.title: Can Tesla Referral Codes Offer a Free FSD Trial?
item.description: A discussion examines the terms of a Tesla referral program and whether an FSD trial might be included, particularly when buying a new car.

item.title: Can Accessories Prevent Tesla Steering-Wheel Alerts?
item.description: The discussion concerns accessories designed to eliminate reminders asking the driver to keep their hands on the steering wheel. One participant questions their usefulness and the reasons for using them.

item.title: FSD Drives the Wrong Way on a One-Way Street
item.description: An owner says that, in FSD mode, their vehicle takes a one-way street in the wrong direction when leaving their driveway and asks how to fix the problem.

item.title: Is the 2027 Model Y AWD Standard Limited to 32 A for Charging?
item.description: An owner asks whether the 2027 Model Y Standard AWD has a 32 A onboard charging limit and where to find that information, particularly in the manual.

item.title: Can Tesla’s 2019 Cameras Be Studied in Depth?
item.description: A member describes the architecture of Tesla’s 2019 cameras, with a small dedicated board transmitting video to the controller via coaxial cable and a proprietary protocol, and asks whether anyone has conducted an in-depth analysis.

item.title: The Tesla Wall Connector Button Does Not Open the Charge Port
item.description: An owner says the button on their Wall Connector does not open the charge port. The discussion includes the Wall Connector version and its antenna receiver.

item.title: What Is the Best Charging Power for a Tesla?
item.description: An owner says they charge at 40 A during off-peak hours on a circuit protected by a 50 A breaker to take advantage of a reduced price per kilowatt-hour.

item.title: Google unveils Intelligent Eyewear, the successor to Google Glass
item.description: These new smart glasses let users use Gemini in everyday life to ask questions, take photos, and translate conversations. Preorders are open, and deliveries will begin on December 10.

item.title: U.S. Justice Department investigates Nvidia
item.description: The Justice Department is conducting three investigations involving Nvidia, including an antitrust proceeding and two others targeting Megaspeed and Supermicro. For now, nothing indicates that criminal charges against Nvidia or Jensen Huang are planned.

item.title: Anthropic launches Fable 5.2 and new workspaces for Claude
item.description: Anthropic has launched Fable 5.2, its model presented as the most powerful to date, along with Claude Sheets, Whiteboard, and Data. These tools offer new ways to work with Claude.

item.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to AI Ultra subscribers
item.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon for AI Ultra subscribers, alongside the release of Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

item.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal decisions
item.description: The Gemini Decisions API, based on the Gemini Decision 1 model, is designed for closed-choice decisions such as tool selection, policy checks, and model routing. It can process up to 1,000 independent questions in a single pass and returns probabilities and confidence scores.

item.title: Gartner forecasts more AI-related job creation than job losses
item.description: Gartner forecasts that AI will create 10.6 million jobs and eliminate 8.9 million by 2030, excluding China and India. Five million additional jobs could be deferred as employers delay hiring to assess AI’s impact.

item.title: The B2A economy puts AI agents at the center of business interactions
item.description: AI agents are driving a platform shift from answering questions to executing complex tasks for users, creating a new “B2A” (Business-to-Agent) economy. Companies that treat agents as priority customers could boost growth, while AI-referred traffic already shows higher engagement and conversion in several industries.

item.title: Claris Harbor aims to turn fleets of Macs into local AI servers
item.description: Apple subsidiary Claris has introduced Harbor, a project designed to turn Macs equipped with Apple Silicon chips into private AI servers. The product could appeal to companies seeking to keep control of their AI workloads locally, but details remain limited.

item.title: Databricks unveils Genie, an autonomous agent for complex enterprise tasks
item.description: Databricks has introduced Genie, an autonomous AI colleague capable of handling long-running tasks, coordinating multiple applications, and following organizational rules. Its components provide shared business context, searches across multiple sources, specialized expertise, and governance of tools, permissions, approvals, and spending.

item.title: Gemini comes to Apple CarPlay worldwide
item.description: Google is rolling out the Gemini app on Apple CarPlay worldwide, allowing iOS users to interact with Gemini Live from their car’s screen. They can prepare for meetings, review briefings and emails, discover local places, and use Gemini to brainstorm or rehearse a presentation.

item.title: Open standards should simplify the development of interoperable AI agents
item.description: Anthropic’s donation of the Model Context Protocol and Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation establishes complementary standards to limit fragmentation in AI agent ecosystems. MCP standardizes real-time connections to tools and data, while Agent Skills progressively loads the procedural knowledge needed.

item.title: AWS Cloud WAN now supports flow logs
item.description: The new feature collects IP addresses, ports, protocols, and traffic volume, among other data. It eliminates the need for users to combine logs from multiple VPCs, accounts, and regions.

item.title: Cognitive science helps developers code better with AI
item.description: Although AI assistants accelerate code generation, developers can rely on cognitive science principles to preserve their understanding and verify results. The article cites the default mode network, spaced repetition, working-memory retrieval, and scientific debugging.

item.title: Edge0 launches a 145-billion-parameter model for personal computers
item.description: Edge0 has open-sourced Edge0-145B, a 145-billion-parameter model designed to run offline on a personal computer, without an account or subscription. The startup claims more than 80 tokens per second, but no independent benchmark is yet available.

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen surpasses Google’s flagship model
item.description: Google DeepMind has announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model designed for coding and agents that outperforms Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis index while costing less. It is available for free in the Gemini app and Google Search.

item.title: AgentRun adds memory and self-improvement to open-source AI agents
item.description: GREP.AI has released AgentRun under the Apache-2.0 license to add memory, crash recovery, and guardrails to agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. With learning enabled, agents can retain notes, skills, and procedures after their missions.

item.title: AI agents mistakenly credited a previously known Maya site as a new discovery
item.description: A team of AI agents analyzed satellite images of Mexico and presented as new a Maya site that had already been identified and published the previous year. Archaeologists criticized the announcements for ignoring scientific literature and local knowledge.

item.title: Runway unveils Solaris, which generates interfaces in real time
item.description: Solaris, Runway’s first “Interface World Model,” draws the screen frame by frame and responds directly to clicks instead of coding an application. Runway also uses it to train agents to navigate unfamiliar websites.

item.title: A cosmological model estimates the age of the universe at 26.7 billion years
item.description: A model proposed by Rajendra Gupta assumes that physical constants evolve slowly and that light loses energy as it travels. It would put the age of the universe at 26.7 billion years, but remains highly marginal and still needs independent verification.

item.title: Phota Labs automatically turns photos into professional-looking shots
item.description: This iOS app, created by two former Adobe employees, scans the camera roll and suggests edited versions of photos. It learns people’s faces to avoid distorting them and adds an invisible watermark to edited images.

item.title: Meta’s Muse agent can call businesses on your behalf
item.description: Muse can now call an insurer, government agency, or restaurant on the user’s behalf. The feature is limited to paying subscribers in the United States, starting at $20 per month.

item.title: ElevenLabs launches Scribe v3 Live to improve voice agents
item.description: Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live transcribe conversations with background noise and multiple speakers. The Live version uses context to determine when a person has finished speaking.

item.title: Nectar automates influencer recruitment for brands
item.description: Nectar’s Creator Agent analyzes more than 300 million profiles, their videos, and partnerships to select and contact creators. It also manages contracts, product shipments, and personalized gifts.

item.title: Google strengthens the privacy protections of its smart glasses
item.description: Google’s glasses equipped with a camera and Gemini display an LED indicator during every capture. If the indicator is covered, photo and video recording is blocked.

item.title: Chinese models appear to bear the fingerprint of Nvidia Blackwell chips
item.description: An analysis of the weights of six Chinese models detected digital traces associated with Nvidia Blackwell chips, which are banned from export to China. The study does not specify where the chips were located or how they may have been obtained.

item.title: Free Chinese AI models can now hack businesses
item.description: According to Israeli startup Tenzai, freely downloadable Chinese models are capable enough to break into corporate networks. Artificial Analysis simultaneously observes that advances in the most advanced models are becoming increasingly expensive.

item.title: Trump proposes Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia
item.description: Donald Trump proposed Tim Cook as Jensen Huang’s successor at the helm of Nvidia. The former Apple executive remains executive chairman of Apple’s board after handing the CEO role to John Ternus.

item.title: Australia wants to require independent audits of frontier AI
item.description: The Australian government is proposing mandatory safety rules for companies developing the most advanced models. A regulator could have these models audited by independent experts and impose penalties.

item.title: Nvidia reportedly confirmed that its AI chips can be geolocated
item.description: Nvidia representatives reportedly said privately that it was technically possible to geolocate its AI chips, as provided for by the Chip Security Act. The U.S. Senate is considering incorporating the bill into its defense budget.

item.title: U.S. senator wants Chinese memory maker CXMT blacklisted
item.description: Senator Tom Cotton is calling for CXMT to be placed on the Commerce Department’s blacklist, which would limit its access to U.S. technologies. The Chinese manufacturer grew from 4% to 10% of the global DRAM market in one year and is developing HBM chips.

item.title: Colette Kress tries to limit Nvidia’s risky bets
item.description: CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim head of Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s departure. According to people close to her, she did not lead major decisions, and Huang often prevailed in disagreements.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s departure could affect Asian manufacturers
item.description: Analysts do not expect a short-term disruption with TSMC, Samsung, or SK Hynix. The main uncertainties concern the long-term product roadmap, which Huang managed directly.

item.title: Chinese laboratories accelerate development of innovative medicines
item.description: Chinese pharmaceutical companies account for at least one-third of innovative drugs in development worldwide and conduct more clinical trials than any other country. They rely primarily on partnerships with Western companies for final development and overseas commercialization.

item.title: Messenger RNA technology opens a new medical chapter
item.description: Messenger RNA technology could produce hundreds of new treatments for various diseases. It can notably create a vaccine against any pathogen in six to eight weeks and could transform treatments for infectious diseases, rare diseases, and cancer.

item.title: AI-generated “slop” is shifting toward design choices
item.description: AI produces significantly less mediocre content, but it has not disappeared. It now appears in design decisions, particularly through poor anticipation of how code will be used and limited reuse of existing libraries.

item.title: Ideas once considered bad are becoming relevant again
item.description: Professional experience gives leaders useful intuitions, but some of them deserve to be reconsidered. Changes in context can make ideas previously considered bad relevant again.

item.title: Employees at AI companies should unionize
item.description: Employees concerned about safety at AI companies could unionize to influence their employers. A union could defend their protections, demand greater transparency, and maintain an independent voice alongside companies’ commitments.

item.title: Google launches Gemini smart glasses starting at $395
item.description: Google has partnered with Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker to create glasses equipped with Gemini. They include a camera and personalized features, along with measures designed to limit intrusive uses.

item.title: China could have ten times more electricity than the United States
item.description: If current trends continue, China will have ten times more electricity than the United States in ten years.

item.title: Age differences influence the acceleration of AI
item.description: Younger people may be less concerned about AI’s ability to extend life. Older people, with less time remaining, have greater incentives to accelerate its development.

item.title: Incident.io details its AI-related spending
item.description: Incident.io’s “effort point” concept is used to analyze AI-related spending.

item.title: Trump mentions Tim Cook as a successor to Jensen Huang
item.description: Donald Trump mentioned Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible successor to Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia. The article highlights his experience succeeding an iconic founder.

item.title: Rust 1.100.0 introduces the never type and new APIs
item.description: The stable Rust 1.100.0 release introduces the never type, the Allocator and DropGuard APIs, and zero-type generation, among other features.

item.title: Companies split over AI agents’ access to commerce
item.description: Amazon, Booking.com, eBay, Target, Resy, Yelp, and other companies are taking different approaches to third-party agents, ranging from blocking them to approving certain platforms. Companies will therefore choose where and how they participate in the agentic web.

item.title: Visa reveals a high failure rate for agent-driven purchases
item.description: Visa’s benchmark found that 42.8% of agent-driven purchasing journeys failed, although some failures still resulted in purchases. Product discovery should therefore not automatically give an agent the power to spend.

item.title: AI reveals that customer loyalty sometimes relied on friction
item.description: AI agents can compare prices, terms, and products every day, threatening loyalty based on customer inertia. Companies must strengthen the value, trust, and experience that remain when comparison becomes easy.

item.title: AI agents are becoming a new distribution channel
item.description: According to McKinsey, large language models can compare far more financial providers than customers previously did. AI removes the friction that protected established players and makes their true loyalty more visible.

item.title: Shopping agents are still making bad decisions
item.description: Visa tested 22 AI models on realistic shopping tasks: 42.8% of executions failed, and 54% of those failures nevertheless resulted in a purchase. AI can therefore remove friction faster than it reduces uncertainty.

item.title: Companies are adopting different strategies toward AI agents
item.description: Retailers, airlines, and platforms are beginning to decide which third-party agents they will accept, limit, or block. This is becoming a strategic choice that determines who can participate in customers’ decisions.

item.title: A Young Founder Named Jensen Huang Benefits from His Namesake’s Troubles
item.description: Jensen Huang, a 24-year-old Singaporean founder, explains why the negative press surrounding Nvidia’s CEO benefits his company.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Departure Does Not Solve Nvidia’s Problems
item.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation begins a period of instability for Nvidia. Its organizational structure and lack of a succession plan leave many problems to resolve.

item.title: Founder Jensen Huang Had Become Nvidia’s Biggest Risk
item.description: Jensen Huang built the Nvidia empire, but the company’s dependence on him has now become a major risk.

item.title: Nvidia’s Structure Complicates Its Transition After Huang’s Departure
item.description: Flat organizations built around powerful founders can be effective, but they become problematic when their leader is gone.

item.title: Small Investors Keep Buying Nvidia Shares
item.description: Despite Nvidia’s stock decline and Wall Street’s pessimism after Jensen Huang’s resignation, some retail investors are taking advantage of the drop to buy more shares.

item.title: Wall Street Analysts Turn Away from Nvidia
item.description: After revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationships and his departure, Wall Street analysts have become more negative on Nvidia’s stock.

item.title: Warby Parker Launches Smart Glasses to Compete with Meta’s
item.description: Warby Parker’s smart glasses use technologies from Google and Samsung. Business Insider tested them to determine how they differ from Meta’s glasses.

item.title: Silicon Valley Prepares for a Future Without Jensen Huang
item.description: At the Cerebral Valley AI Summit, founders and investors warned that Huang’s departure could hurt startups and destabilize an industry that views Nvidia as its “central bank.”

item.title: The United States Faces a Growing Population Shortage
item.description: Falling birth rates, immigration and tourism are creating a “Great People Shortage.” Areas dependent on newcomers are expected to feel the effects first.

item.title: TikTok Centralizes Its U.S. E-Commerce Operations in China
item.description: TikTok has placed its U.S. e-commerce operations under the responsibility of Chinese executives. Business Insider obtained the organizational chart for the 14 top executives and their teams.

item.title: Instacart Partners with Provi to Supply Bars
item.description: Instacart has partnered with Provi. The platform will offer same-day delivery to bars and restaurants for nonalcoholic items such as mixers and garnishes.

item.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Email for Many Companies
item.description: A Microsoft outage is disrupting email, even as some business executives use it very little.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Leather Jackets Have Become a Joke
item.description: Jensen Huang’s once-iconic leather jackets are now being mocked following the controversies surrounding the Nvidia leader.

item.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool to Address Labor Shortages
item.description: Anthropic is offering a new Claude tool designed to help manufacturers facing labor shortages.

item.title: Flowers Left Outside Nvidia Headquarters After Huang’s Resignation
item.description: Photos show flowers left outside Nvidia headquarters following Jensen Huang’s resignation.

item.title: Amazon’s Ring Flying Camera Raises Questions About Its Target Audience
item.description: The Amazon Ring Drone Cam product has prompted questions about who it is intended for.

item.title: Michael Burry Advises Selling Nvidia Stock
item.description: Investor Michael Burry recommends getting out of Nvidia stock.

item.title: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s Cousin, Leads Nvidia Rival AMD
item.description: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s cousin, is the CEO of AMD, an Nvidia competitor.

item.title: Alice Huang Barred from Returning to Singapore
item.description: Singapore says Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive involved in the Nvidia scandal, is not permitted to return to the country.

item.title: RLHF Is Costly Mainly Because of Its Training Loop
item.description: In RLHF, the infrastructure costs of maintaining four models simultaneously during PPO can exceed annotation expenses. DPO reuses the same preference data without a separate reward model, making it a simpler starting point for most teams.

item.title: Cerebras Reports $230.9 Million in Third-Quarter Revenue
item.description: Cerebras reported $230.9 million in third-quarter revenue, up 70%, and raised its full-year guidance.

item.title: FBI Dismantles North Korean Cryptocurrency Theft Campaign
item.description: The FBI disrupted North Korea’s FaceStealer campaign, which used fake Zoom-style meetings featuring recordings of people known to the victims to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency.

item.title: Google Prepares Gemini Glasses with Translation in More Than 70 Languages
item.description: Google announced Gemini glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster offering hands-free navigation and translation in more than 70 languages. They will be sold starting at $395 in the United States and South Korea, with in-store availability beginning December 10.

item.title: Yogurt Summarizes Calls Without Sending a Bot to the Meeting
item.description: Yogurt records calls without having a bot join the meeting, then produces a free summary with next steps assigned to each person. The project is presented as free and open source.

item.title: Pomerado Turns API-Less Websites into Tools for Coding Agents
item.description: Pomerado turns a website without an API, such as a vendor invoice portal, into a tool that a coding agent can use from a single prompt. The service offers a free plan followed by a $50-per-month option.

item.title: Kiln Runs AI Models Directly in the Browser
item.description: Kiln runs conversational, transcription and image models directly in the browser from Hugging Face files, without a server or conversion step. The project is presented as free and open source.

item.title: Spotify DJ Adds Nine Voices and an Option to Turn Off Commentary
item.description: Spotify Premium DJ offers nine new voices and a setting to disable most commentary between songs while retaining personalized recommendations.

item.title: Disney Expands Adobe Partnership for Its Parks, Films and ESPN Content
item.description: Disney is using Adobe’s custom Firefly Foundry models to speed up art design, visual effects and ESPN content. The shorter iteration times also raise questions about work methods and staffing.

item.title: Google Gemini Shows What It Remembers About Users and Lets Them Correct It
item.description: Gemini displays and lets users edit the information it remembers about them in a summary organized into five timestamped categories. However, deleting a memory may not erase the source conversation.

item.title: Microsoft Teams rolls out AI detection of phishing attempts
item.description: Microsoft Teams is rolling out AI-powered detection of impersonation and social engineering in chats, even without a malicious link. Warnings about deepfakes in meetings will follow, but will require third-party configuration.

item.title: Southeast Asian anti-scam hub offers free training
item.description: The Scam Ready ASEAN hub offers free training, an interactive game and country-specific reporting contacts across 11 nations. Scams cost Southeast Asia $23.6 billion.

item.title: Meta AI: features, pricing and user guide
item.description: Meta AI is integrated into Meta’s apps, with features powered by Muse, multiple pricing tiers and privacy controls. The guide covers platform availability and use of Incognito mode, among other topics.

item.title: Part 5: Automating repetitive tasks with AI
item.description: The final part of the playbook explains how to document your system, connect beehiiv to AI, and automate recurring tasks. It also shows how to turn the most engaged readers into customers and build a prompt library.

item.title: Guide: Creating a B2B newsletter that generates leads
item.description: This guide explains how to write for an ideal customer, use your newsletter as a CRM, and measure leads rather than just opens.
